ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, ss. 1, 21C, 21E and 28A (as amended by FIC Amendment Act 1 of 2017 and General Laws (AML/CFT) Amendment Act 22 of 2022); Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss. 26(5), 50(3) and 56(4)-(5); Companies Regulations 2011, reg. 32; mandatory CIPC beneficial ownership filing effective 1 April 2023 (Form CoR 40.2 and UBO register); Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 (commenced 27 December 2024); FATF Recommendations 24-25; detailed guidance in FIC Guidance Notes 8A and 12. Disclosure thresholds: 5% beneficial interest for the CIPC register; 25% equity ownership or control for FIC AML identification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each ultimate beneficial owner and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization at the South African embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for each shareholder and UBO (identity verification and AML standing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Utility bill or lease agreement as proof of residential address of each director (issued within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal utility, licensed service provider, or landlord in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized resolution of the foreign corporate shareholder authorizing incorporation and appointing directors of the South African entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residency certificate or tax identification document for each ultimate beneficial owner (FATCA/CRS due diligence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Revenue authority of the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based due diligence for all UBOs, directors and authorised signatories under FIC Act s. 21; real-time screening against the FIC targeted financial sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN and consolidated non-SDN lists (required because Mercury and Stripe run through US payment rails), EU consolidated sanctions list, and UK OFSI consolidated list; PEP status, whether domestic or foreign, triggers senior management approval and source-of-wealth verification per FIC Guidance Note 8A; screening must occur at onboarding and on a continuous basis thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services portal (eservices.cipc.co.za) - Name Reservation and Company Registration module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be submitted in English or Afrikaans; official-language names not written in Latin script must be transliterated into Latin characters. The name must comply with s. 11(1)-(2) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, must not be offensive or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or trademark, and must include the mandatory suffix '(Pty) Ltd'. Tokens such as 'International' or 'Global' require documentary proof of cross-border operations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 6 months and may be renewed once for a further 6 months before expiry via the CIPC e-Services portal. Upon rejection, the applicant may, within 10 business days, file an objection under Companies Regulation 16 or lodge a fresh application accompanied by ministerial or regulatory consent letters for sensitive tokens. Refusals may be reviewed by the Companies Tribunal under s. 160 of the Companies Act, with subsequent recourse to the High Court within the applicable review window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A serviced virtual office is acceptable for this cloud-software business provided it maintains a genuine physical South African street address, daily mail handling and statutory service-of-process capacity. A PO Box, mail-forwarding-only address or purely non-physical address is unlawful under s. 23(3) of the Companies Act and constitutes a CIPC compliance breach. No industry-specific physical-premises licence applies to ISIC 6201.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated 5%-10% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by CIPC or SARS for a FATF low-risk, non-licensed cloud-services entity; probability escalates upon sanctions/PEP alerts, material cross-border transactions, or lapse of annual return filings.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended; particularly ss. 13–15 (incorporation and registration), s. 19 (legal personality), s. 40 (consideration for shares), s. 66 (board of directors), and the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Department of Trade, Industry and Competition
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1A – Standard, or CoR 15.1B – Custom)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued for nil or nominal par value. No escrow or deposit account requirement. Consideration must be determined by the board in accordance with s. 40 of the Companies Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The subscribers to the Memorandum of Incorporation are hereby allotted shares in the number and class set out in the subscriber schedule, effective as of the date of incorporation. 2. The registered office of the Company is adopted as [physical address], and the postal address as recorded in the Notice of Incorporation is adopted. 3. The following persons are appointed as directors and officers: [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Company Secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting. 4. The directors are authorized to open a corporate bank account, register with the South African Revenue Service, and execute all necessary filings to commence business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the CIPC e-Services portal, complete the name reservation application (CoR 9.1), select a unique name with the suffix '(Pty) Ltd', and pay the prescribed fee. The name is screened against existing registered names and trademarks.
required_dossiers: Applicant identity document (South African ID or passport)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or reserved with conditions, file a revised name application or submit an objection within 30 days online via the CIPC e-Services portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors and an CIPC-accredited incorporation practitioner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) in accordance with the Companies Act, specifying share classes, director powers, and governance rules. Complete the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1). Ensure all subscribers and initial directors execute or authorise the documents.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of directors' identity documents
Particulars of share structure and subscriber consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any drafting inconsistencies, re-execute the documents, and resubmit to the CIPC before the underlying name reservation expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal – Company Registration window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the signed Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) and the MOI, attach the reserved name reference and the proposed registered office address, and pay the incorporation fee of R175 (approx. USD 10). CIPC will issue a Certificate of Incorporation and an Enterprise Number.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of incorporators and directors
Proof of physical and postal address for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a query, respond via the e-Services portal within 15 business days, amend the identified defect, and resubmit. Appeal an unjustified refusal through the CIPC internal dispute resolution process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Tax Registrations (Income Tax, VAT, PAYE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – eFiling portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax using the COR101.1 form. Simultaneously apply for VAT if projected turnover exceeds R1 million per annum, and for Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) as an employer.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of directors and the accounting officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS requests additional information, respond within the stipulated 30-day period. Submit missing forms through eFiling and verify registration status via the SARS interactive voice response service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (DEL) – district office or online platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) using form UI-8, and apply for a letter of good standing under the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA).
required_dossiers: List of initial directors and proposed employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is incomplete or rejected, re-submit corrected information with supporting affidavits and obtain written confirmation from the department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Local Municipal Business Licensing and Corporate Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality (e.g., City of Johannesburg) and commercial bank of choice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a general business licence or premises permit from the municipal authority if the company occupies a physical office. Open a corporate bank account with a Tier-1 bank for operational funding and investor capital. No sectoral license is needed for software development.
required_dossiers: Bank account application forms and director KYC documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal zoning or license approval is queried, obtain a consent use certificate from the local town planning department and reapply. For banking, satisfy the bank's enhanced due diligence requests and re-submit the account application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No dedicated industrial licensing board for software publishing; the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (DTIC) and the local Municipality supervise general business premises compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating license required; a general business licence may be issued by the city/municipality under the Business Act 71 of 1991 for the physical office premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) – provincial environmental authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category 3 (Listing Notice 3) does not apply to office-based software publishing; a formal EIA is not required. The company may obtain a Registration/Exemption certificate if requested by the provincial authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC emissions. Compliance with SANS 10400-AA (water supply) and SANS 10400-RA (stormwater drainage) if applicable to the office premises. Waste disposal handled in accordance with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the local Fire and Rescue Services after a pre-occupation inspection; structural load inspection in accordance with SANS 10400 if required by the building's age; Certificate of Occupancy for the premises. Additionally, a workplace compliance clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 is necessary for employee safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — eFiling portal at https://www.sarsefiling.co.za; official website at https://www.sars.gov.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned entity must first complete company registration through the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC). The company then registers for income tax via SARS eFiling, and SARS issues an income tax reference number. For VAT, the taxpayer submits Form VAT101 through SARS eFiling within 21 days after the VAT registration threshold is exceeded. Non-resident or foreign-owned entities must file through an appointed SARS representative or registered tax practitioner with a power of attorney, and provide CIPC registration certificate (CoR 14.3), Memorandum of Incorporation, director identification, proof of address and banking details as requested by SARS. SARS then issues a VAT vendor number upon approval.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box entity classification regime. A (Pty) Ltd incorporated or effectively managed in South Africa is a resident company subject to entity-level tax on worldwide income. Available statutory elections include VAT group vendor registration under s50 of the VAT Act, CFC high-tax exemption elections under s9D(9) of the Income Tax Act, and certain corporate restructuring rollover elections. Hybrid mismatch anti-avoidance rules apply compulsorily and cannot be opted out through unilateral classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration: ZAR 1,000,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period. Voluntary registration: permitted where taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 in a 12-month period. Foreign suppliers of electronic services have a mandatory registration threshold of ZAR 50,000 in South African- sourced turnover under s23A of the VAT Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS has not implemented a continuous transaction control or real-time fiscal clearance mandate. Electronic tax invoices are valid if they contain the prescribed VAT particulars and preserve data integrity and authenticity under the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act 25 of 2002. No mandatory API approval or digital stamping is currently required; VAT returns and electronic schedules are filed periodically through SARS eFiling, and SARS may require supporting XML or electronic records during audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated under s11(1)(a) of the VAT Act if supplied to a non-resident, physically exported from South Africa through the customs export process, and exported within the prescribed period after the tax invoice is issued (generally 90 days), with retained documentary evidence. Services are zero-rated under s11(2) when supplied to a non-resident who is outside South Africa at the time of supply and the services are not used or consumed in South Africa. Cloud infrastructure, database hosting, API monitoring and DevOps tools supplied to offshore customers are eligible if the direct recipient is a non-resident and the services are not consumed in South Africa.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice / VAT tax invoice showing 0% VAT
Bill of lading or airway bill evidencing physical export
Proof of physical delivery and export acceptance at the South African customs point
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank advice evidencing foreign exchange receipt from the non-resident purchaser
Written supply or sale contract stating the export terms (FOB / CFR / CIF)
Export packing list and relevant cargo or transport documentation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may retrospectively reassess a zero-rated export if the supporting evidence is deficient, irregular or fraudulent. The exporter is then liable for output VAT at 15%, interest under s187 of the Tax Administration Act, and understatement penalties under s222 of the Tax Administration Act. Intentional false zero-rating or fraudulent refund claims may result in criminal prosecution, fines and imprisonment. SARS retains an unlimited prescription period in cases of fraud or evasion, and failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days may trigger separate South African Reserve Bank exchange-control penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933), the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, and the SARB Exchange Control Rulings and Currency and Exchanges Manual.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa operates a partially convertible currency regime with formal distinction between current and capital account transactions. Current account payments, including trade and service-related cross-border settlements, are generally permitted through an Authorised Dealer without SARB FinSurv approval, subject to documentary verification. Capital account transactions, including equity injections, acquisition of local assets by non-residents, and restructuring, require Authorised Dealer sign-off within delegated authority or SARB FinSurv prior approval. Profit remittances by a non-resident-owned South African (Pty) Ltd are permissible but subject to compliance with the Investment Reconciliation Form, annual financial statements demonstrating distributable reserves, a valid SARS tax clearance, and formal bank reporting. Dividends may be repatriated through an Authorised Dealer, but the company must ensure no inconsistent 'loop structure' exists and that the original inward capital was properly declared and recorded with the SARB. Branch profits similarly require audited accounts and tax compliance. Capital convertibility is therefore not absolute: each transfer is subject to documentary validity, anti-money-laundering checks, and exchange control reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received in South Africa within 180 days from the date of export. The exporter must surrender the full export proceeds to an Authorised Dealer, meaning the foreign currency proceeds must be converted into ZAR unless a foreign currency account or retention arrangement was specifically approved by SARB FinSurv. The mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts is 100% where no approved foreign currency account is held. For services exports, which include cloud-based DevTools infrastructure, the carrier or service provider must receive payment through the South African banking channel within 180 days of the invoice date or service completion date. The exporter must submit an export declaration, invoice, proof of receipt, and any supporting contracts to the Authorised Dealer for exchange control purposes. Non-compliance can lead to penalties, suspension from operating a foreign currency account, and criminal exposure under the Exchange Control Regulations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
First National Bank (a division of FirstRand Bank Limited)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium as a primary clearing rail and Medium as a supplementary settlement tool. Foreign digital EMIs such as Mercury and Stripe Treasury are not licensed as South African Authorised Dealers, cannot process ZAR-denominated exchange control reporting, and cannot independently satisfy SARB FinSurv requirements for capital entries or trade payments. They may be used for segregated offshore collection of USD/EUR/GBP subscription revenues from international customers, provided the funds are subsequently swept into the South African operating account through a SARB-approved banking channel. Any EMI receiving funds from South African customers or making payments into South Africa without an appropriate authorised-dealer partnership may constitute unauthorised cross-border money transmission. Therefore, the primary corporate banking relationship must be with a Tier-1 South African commercial bank; the EMI can serve only as a treasury sub-ledger for offshore SaaS billing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and beneficial owners are generally required to complete an in-person identity verification and compliance interview at a branch of the South African bank for initial corporate onboarding. Some banks allow a hybrid process with a remote online interview followed by notarised/apostilled original documents, but fully remote opening for a non-resident-owned (Pty) Ltd is rarely permitted. The company must present certified passports of all directors and shareholders, proof of residential address, a board resolution resolving the account opening and mandated signatories, the Memorandum of Incorporation, Certificate of Incorporation, beneficial ownership register, and a SARS tax clearance or proof of registration. Banks may also require an introduction letter from a corresponding relationship bank and audited or independently prepared financials where the shareholder structure is complex.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident controlling shareholder with no local economic substance or physical presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution appointing an independent local director or authorised representative; organisational chart; physical office lease agreement in South Africa; company tax registration with SARS; SARS tax clearance certificate; payroll and employee tax records where employees are locally hired; business plan; current customer contracts; evidence of local operational expenditure; and periodic board minutes showing local management discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume inbound API/cloud subscription payments from anonymous or fragmented end users
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated customer due diligence and merchant KYC records; Stripe/Mercury settlement statements; source-of-funds evidence; transaction monitoring and behavioural analytics policy; detailed service agreements with enterprise customers; IP ownership and licensing documentation; export invoices under the correct ISIC 6201 / services classification; and an internal AML risk assessment manual.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: CRS/FATCA classification mismatches and perceived US permanent establishment arising from use of US EMIs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRS self-certification forms for all controlling persons; IRS Form W-8BEN-E confirming no US trade or business; ownership and consolidated group structure chart; correspondence with the South African Authorised Dealer regarding the US EMI arrangement; evidence that agreements are entered into by the South African entity; and a declaration of no US PE for tax purposes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Broad discretion to make international payments to unrelated suppliers or vendors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vendor onboarding policy; procurement contracts; purchase orders; supplier invoices matching cloud infrastructure, software licensing, and database hosting services; SWIFT beneficiary due diligence files; sanctions screening confirmations; dual-control payment procedure; and evidence that all cross-border payments flow through the SARB-authorised channel with Form A.1 or equivalent declarations where applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Recommended routing is a verified SWIFT MT103 transfer from the non-resident shareholder's offshore bank to the South African (Pty) Ltd's designated capital or operational account at a Tier-1 SARB-authorised commercial bank. The foreign currency transfer should use an accepted inward payment purpose code corresponding to 'Foreign direct investment in South Africa' or 'Capital increase by non-resident'. The bank must receive the board resolution, updated Memorandum of Incorporation, proof of share allotment, and a completed foreign investment declaration (Form FA1 or equivalent). The Authorised Dealer will enter the inward capital onto the South African Reserve Bank reporting system and issue an inward payment reference for use in future dividend remittances. The funds must be recorded on an Investment Reconciliation Form, which becomes the baseline for profit repatriation. No ZAR conversion or offshore account should be used without explicit SARB approval; all foreign capital inflows should remain identifiable and traceable to the corporate banking ledger.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for trade-related cloud infrastructure, data-centre bandwidth, software licences, and subcontracting services should be settled through SWIFT MT103 or commercial letters of credit. For straightforward supplier payments below Authorised Dealer thresholds, corporate internet banking with an approved foreign-exchange deal slip is acceptable; larger or regular payments require Form A.1 and supporting contracts/invoices. Recommended SARB payment purpose codes include '3610 – Computer and processing services', '3620 – Cloud computing services', '3501 – Data processing, storage and hosting services', and '3205 – Computer software licensing fees', as appropriate. Domestic ZAR legs should settle through the South African clearing system, while cross-border legs will use SWIFT. Commercial LC instruments are appropriate only for physical equipment purchases embedded in DevTools infrastructure expansion, and must be opened through the South African commercial bank with sight or usance terms supported by the underlying procurement contract.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts (FX forwards) with a South African Authorised Dealer for firm commercial commitments, generally up to 12 months, with rollover on documented underlying exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on ZAR/USD or ZAR/EUR executed with approved counterparties, used where physical ZAR settlement is not commercially practical

Cross-currency swaps and interest-rate currency swaps under an ISDA Master Agreement with an approved South African or offshore bank, subject to SARB FinSurv approval requirements and documented treasury risk policy
Plain-vanilla FX swaps combining spot and forward legs, limited to managing near-term ZAR/USD liquidity mismatches in the operating account

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under Companies Act 71 of 2008, sec. 33
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties accrue monthly; non-compliance notices may be issued; two consecutive years of default expose the company to administrative strike-off under sec. 82(4)(b).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation submitted with the Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due concurrently with the Annual Return; any beneficial ownership change caused by a share transfer must be filed within 14 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update beneficial ownership data is a statutory offence; repeated non-compliance may lead to compliance notices and deregistration of the company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is compulsory if the public interest score exceeds 350, if required by the Companies Regulations for certain licences, or if the company is not owner-controlled. Owner-controlled private companies with a public interest score below 350 may file an independent review instead of a full audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public interest entities; IFRS for SMEs for other entities unless the company is required by its Memorandum of Incorporation or by CIPC to apply full IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The beneficial ownership register must be maintained at the registered office and an annual confirmation must be included in the CIPC Annual Return. Any shareholding transfer that changes beneficial ownership must be recorded and submitted to CIPC within 14 days. There is no notarisation requirement, but the annual confirmation duty is continuous and requires accurate, up-to-date UBO data.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $2,000 - $5,500 per year depending on corporate complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday; principal preferential deductions include the Research and Development tax incentive (additional 50% deduction on qualifying R&D expenditure), the Learnership Allowance, and the Special Economic Zone (SEZ) 15% corporate rate. The s12H employment incentive is also available.
